title: Interfacility transfer: intracerebral haemorrhage
stem: Resus. Mr Yip, 60, has sudden left-sided weakness. GCS 11 (E3V3M5). Your hospital has no neurosurgery; the tertiary centre has accepted him. Review the CT, prepare him for transfer and manage problems on the way.

phases.title: CT and bloods
phases.goal: What is it, and what must be reversed?

phases.title: Stabilise
phases.goal: The blood pressure target from the cart, and the airway plan.

phases.title: Prepare the transfer
phases.goal: People, kit, drugs, documents, the receiving team.

phases.title: En route
phases.goal: Deterioration in the ambulance: recognise, evaluate, support.

review.text: Needle decompression site. Your notes use the 2nd intercostal space, mid-clavicular line. ATLS 10th and 11th use the 4th/5th space just anterior to the mid-axillary line in adults (2nd space mid-clavicular line in children).
Reintubation in the ambulance. Your notes say it is not recommended. Better: ventilate with a bag-mask or supraglottic airway first, and reintubate only if needed and safe, with the vehicle stopped.

notes:
Checked against the Association of Anaesthetists interhospital transfer guideline (2019), the Intensive Care Society transfer guidance (2019), NICE NG128 stroke (2019, updated 2022), AHA/ASA spontaneous ICH guideline (2022), and ATLS 10th.

Preparation (your 8 points match): communication (patient/family, receiving team, transport team, ambulance), documentation, consent, equipment/kit (monitoring, suction, oxygen with reserve, drugs pre-drawn and labelled), pre-transport assessment and stabilisation (secure airway if GCS ≤8, falling GCS, or airway at risk; two IV lines; tubes and lines secured), appropriate escort (critical → doctor plus nurse). ICH specifics: SBP target 130–140 within an hour if presenting within 6 hours with SBP 150–220 (NICE; AHA 140, avoid under 130), reverse anticoagulation, head up 30°, glucose normal, treat seizures. Deterioration uses your REST approach (Recognise, Evaluate, Support, Transport); for the intubated patient, DOPES.

Differences from your notes: (1) needle decompression — your notes say 2nd ICS midclavicular; ATLS 10th recommends the 4th/5th ICS just anterior to the mid-axillary line in adults (2nd ICS MCL for children). (2) 'Reintubation not recommended' in the ambulance: better to say ventilate with a bag-mask or supraglottic airway first and reintubate only if needed and safe (stop the vehicle).

Perfect script checked against the ICS/AAGBI transfer guidance and AHA 2022 ICH, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed over-lowering the BP and sending him with a porter; ACCEPT-style preparation spoken.

Support: stop the ambulance; RSI with pre-drawn drugs; ETCO2 4.5–5

badge.name: Safe Passage
badge.flavor: Stabilise before you go. Twice the oxygen. REST, then DOPES.

options: A single nurse with an airway kit
A porter and a healthcare assistant
Half the calculated need, plus a spare
Reverse with PCC and vitamin K
Add aspirin 300 mg for the stroke

script.say: CT head. Clotting, FBC, glucose, U&E. Anticoagulant history. A right deep intracerebral haemorrhage with intraventricular extension.
script.do: Hyperdense haematoma in the right basal ganglia/thalamus with blood in the lateral ventricle. "A right deep intracerebral haemorrhage with intraventricular extension." INR 1.0, platelets 210, glucose 7.1. No anticoagulants.

script.say: Labetalol 10–20 mg IV boluses to a systolic of 130–140.
Airway: GCS 11 and protecting it, so no intubation now; but his escort must be able to intubate, with RSI drugs pre-drawn and labelled.

Communication: his family, the receiving neurosurgeon, the transport team and the ambulance; ETA agreed. Documentation: his condition, treatment, vital signs and plan; a copy of the CT and the notes. The risks and benefits explained to his family, and their agreement.
Transport kit: monitor, suction, oxygen for twice the journey, and drugs. A critical transfer: a doctor and a nurse escort him.
Recognise: GCS 7, right pupil dilated, HR falling. Evaluate: airway, breathing, glucose. Support: stop the ambulance; RSI with pre-drawn drugs; ETCO2 4.5–5.
Transport: inform the receiving team; consider hypertonic saline or mannitol per neurosurgeon.
The ventilator alarms: DOPES. Disconnect; bag with 100% oxygen. Displacement: tube mark, ETCO2 trace, bilateral air entry. Obstruction: pass a suction catheter.
script.do: Easy to bag. Saturation climbs. Tube at 22 cm, trace present, equal air entry. Thick secretions cleared.

script.say: Pneumothorax: chest rise, trachea. Equipment: oxygen supply, circuit, ventilator.
